subject.title: feat: enable the new exec approvals pipeline behind an opt-in setting

question: Should Windows ship a hidden `settings.json`-only switch that activates fail-closed V2 exec approvals before prompt UI is available?
rationale: The patch can support multiple rollout strategies, but deciding whether this experimental command-authorization boundary is supportable and discoverable enough to ship requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Gate on rollout readiness
options.body: Keep the PR open until a maintainer approves the rollout shape and current-head gateway-to-node MXC proof is available.

options.title: Approve developer-only opt-in
options.body: Accept the hidden switch as an explicitly experimental surface with operator documentation and owned prompt-UI follow-up work.

options.title: Wait for complete approvals UX
options.body: Defer production wiring until prompt handling and the intended operator workflow can land with it.

recommendation.title: Gate on rollout readiness
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until a maintainer approves the rollout shape and current-head gateway-to-node MXC proof is available.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier exec-approval security work provides the strongest available history signal for ownership of this rollout-boundary decision.
